name: Delegate Manager
description: Advertise application-defined delegation roles, manage interfaces registered for those roles, and record role-scoped preferences. Each role carries the actual unbound interfaces an application accepts, as alternatives. A caller supplies an actual OpenBindings interface value and one or more roles; registration admits the interface for every requested role atomically. Registration identity is manager-local, not an identity or location of the interface. Higher preference expresses stronger caller preference within a role, not a mandatory selection algorithm. The application owns role-specific eligibility, configuration, selection, invocation, and lifecycle policy. This interface defines neither document retrieval, external interface discovery, nor a generic delegation execution protocol.

DelegateRole.description: An application-defined responsibility for which interfaces may be registered. A role is local to the manager's scope; it is not an authorization role, an operation identifier, a binding specification, or a new OpenBindings Core concept.

id.description: Opaque role identifier, unique in this manager's scope. Compared exactly; no global role vocabulary or identifier format is prescribed. An existing identifier must not be reassigned to an unrelated responsibility.

description.description: The responsibility's purpose and application-owned admission and use rules. Explain the effect of enrollment, multiple registrations, preferences (including whether and when they affect selection and how ties are handled), built-in implementations, provider changes, and absence or failure of an eligible delegate. This is human-readable documentation, not an executable policy language.

acceptedInterfaces.description: Alternative expected interfaces, carried as actual OBI values, not locations or interface-name assertions. Each must be a valid unbound OBI with at least one operation and no dependency entries. All operations in one alternative are the required capability set for that alternative. A candidate must correspond to and be schema-compatible with at least one complete alternative; it may carry additional operations. Array order is not a preference. These meanings are defined by this manager interface, not by Core. Expected bindings, dependency declarations, or operation names alone must not be used as proof that a candidate can safely be invoked.

DelegateRoleIds.description: A nonempty set of role identifiers, carried as an array. Entries must be distinct, with exact string equality; duplicates are invalid. Array order carries no meaning or priority. Each role is selected explicitly by the caller; matching an unrequested role does not enroll the interface for it.

DelegateRolePreferences.description: Explicit preferences keyed by exact enrolled role ID. Every key must belong to this registration's roles; an unlisted role is invalid, not an implicit enrollment. Missing entries have effective preference zero. Values are finite JSON numbers, preserved without silent rounding; larger values express stronger preference between registrations in the same role and manager scope. Equal values express no ordering. Magnitude is not a weight, probability, permission, mandatory failover order, or comparison across roles. The application's documented role policy determines how preference affects use. An explicitly supplied zero must remain an explicit entry until changed, cleared, or its role membership or registration is removed. It is distinct as stored data from an absent entry, but has the same effective preference. These are not preferences on the carried OBI's bindings.

DelegateRegistration.description: One manager-local enrollment of an interface value in one or more roles. The same interface may occur in several registrations, and several registrations may occupy the same role subject to that role's rules. Listing a registration reports recorded enrollment, not current health, trust, authorization, binding support, selection, or proof of implementation behavior.

id.description: Opaque manager-assigned registration identifier. Unique and not reused within this manager's scope, including after removal. This is not the interface's identity, a locator, or an authorization credential.

interface.description: The complete supplied OBI value retained for this registration. Preserve its declared values, including extensions and the schema, source, binding, and transform graphs; textual formatting is not significant. The manager must not replace it with a summary, locator, or silently refreshed remote document. Retaining this value does not freeze resources or services it references.

roles.description: The complete recorded set of roles for this registration. Matching an additional role does not implicitly add it. Each role's configuration and selection remain independent; shared registration does not imply shared credentials, namespace, trust, or permission.

rolePreferences.description: The complete explicit preference map for this registration. Empty when none are set. Listing must not synthesize explicit entries for roles using the implicit zero default.

openbindings.delegate-manager.listRoles.description: Return a complete, internally consistent snapshot of the roles the application currently advertises in this manager's scope. Role identifiers must be unique. Empty when no roles are offered. Expected interfaces are returned by value. Listing does not invoke providers, fetch a provider document, create roles, or register anything. Implementations must not silently truncate this result; inability to produce the complete result is an unsuccessful invocation.

roles.description: All advertised roles. Order is unspecified and has no selection semantics.

openbindings.delegate-manager.registerDe.description: Enroll the supplied interface value for every requested role. Without id, allocate a fresh registration identity; no deduplication by interface value, name, location, or role is implied. With id, atomically replace that existing registration's complete interface and role set while retaining its identity; an unknown or removed id fails and must not create or resurrect a registration. Validate the supplied OBI and all requested roles against the role definitions current at commit. For each role, establish operation-name/alias correspondence with at least one complete accepted interface; that correspondence is the provider's compatibility claim, and directional schema comparison looks for a contradiction of it. For this whole-interface admission check, each expected operation's key is looked up exactly in the provider's key/alias namespace, following the shared-interface correspondence convention. Aliases on the expected operation are retained but are not additional required names or substitutes for its key in this check. Treat the expected interface as target and the provider as candidate: provider input schemas must accommodate expected inputs, and provider output schemas must satisfy expected outputs. See the Delegate Manager README's Compatibility reference for the existing authorities and comparison-procedure boundary. An established contradiction refuses admission; a comparison the manager cannot decide leaves the claim standing. Extra provider operations are permitted and must not gain enrollment or authority. When rolePreferences is supplied, it replaces the complete explicit preference map and may contain only requested roles. When omitted on new enrollment, store an empty map; when omitted on re-enrollment, preserve the current explicit preferences for retained roles and discard those for removed roles. Added roles have implicit zero preference unless explicitly supplied. Interface, roles, and preferences commit atomically. A rejection before commit leaves no new registration and preserves an existing registration unchanged; no partial mutation may commit. Failure to observe completion, including loss of a response after commit, does not prove rejection or rollback: commit status may be unknown to the caller. The operation does not invoke provider work, automatically migrate data, or activate new trust/secret delivery merely because the interface changed. Its successful output is the committed registration. Interface and roles are full replacement, not a patch; omission of rolePreferences has the separately stated preservation meaning. This operation is not declared idempotent: a call without id creates a fresh record and must not be blindly retried after an uncertain outcome. Fetching an interface document from a caller-supplied location is not part of this operation.

id.description: When supplied, the existing registration to re-enroll with the supplied interface and complete role set. Omit for a new registration. Passing an unknown id fails.

interface.description: The actual provider OBI value. It may come from memory, a file, synthesis, another operation, or caller-managed retrieval; no published address is required. The provider's own dependencies, if present, are not automatically satisfied by registration.

rolePreferences.description: Optional complete explicit preference map, committed atomically with enrollment. An empty object clears all explicit preferences. If omitted, a new registration has none; re-enrollment preserves current preferences for retained roles only.

openbindings.delegate-manager.listDelega.description: Return a complete, internally consistent snapshot of registrations in this manager's scope, including their actual retained interface values and complete explicit rolePreferences. When role is supplied, include only registrations whose recorded roles contain that exact identifier; the filter does not alter their returned role sets or preference maps. A filter need not name a currently advertised role, so old enrollments remain discoverable after role changes. Empty when none match. Registration identifiers must be unique. Order is unspecified and does not imply preference. Listing reports recorded enrollment and caller preferences, not a live eligibility or invocation decision. Implementations must not silently truncate the result; inability to produce the complete result is an unsuccessful invocation.

role.description: Optional exact role identifier by which to filter registrations. Omit to list all registrations.

openbindings.delegate-manager.setDelegat.description: Set or clear the explicit preference of one existing registration in one of its recorded roles. The registration ID must exist and the exact role must be in its recorded role set; otherwise fail without mutation, even when clearing. A number sets that role's explicit preference; null removes its explicit entry, restoring effective zero. Preserve every other preference, the interface value, and all role memberships. The mutation is atomic with respect to enrollment, removal, and other preference changes; it must not recreate a removed registration or leave a preference for a removed role. This operation may edit an existing membership whose role is no longer advertised, but does not reactivate the role or confer eligibility. Higher means stronger caller preference within this role and manager scope; it does not mandate selection, authorize invocation, select a binding, retry work, or migrate state. The application must follow its documented role policy for interpreting preferences. No provider work is invoked by this operation. Repeating the same set or clear is idempotent; no stale-write protection is implied.

role.description: Exact role ID already recorded on this registration.

preference.description: Finite JSON number to set as the explicit role preference, or null to clear it. Omission is invalid; zero is a stored preference, not a clear request.

openbindings.delegate-manager.unregister.description: Ensure that the registration identified by id is absent from this manager's scope, removing all its recorded role memberships and preferences together. An absent id succeeds. Removal must prevent the record from being offered by subsequent registration lookups; it does not promise cancellation of in-flight work, revocation of upstream credentials, deletion or migration of provider data, or removal of another registration that carries the same interface. Those effects require separately defined application lifecycle behavior. To retain some roles, re-enroll the existing id with the desired nonempty role set instead.

id.description: The manager-local registration identifier to remove.
